summary:
Fix round 1 for the rings lane is finished. The lane started at v1 plus the lead's hotfix (LANE, MAIN and lanes2/hotfix were md5-equal).

BLOCKER (ring A's opening pulsed closed): the lead's hotfix fixes it. I did not re-implement or touch it, and verified it with fresh captures and the judge's own aclose.py. For presses at tau 0, 0.6, 1.3, 2.6 and 3.3 the opening share is 1.00 at F404, F420 and F436. A stays at 0.59994-0.60004 m from t+3.43 s until the release in every hold, including a 20 s hold. There is no dip anywhere; the judge had measured 0.15-0.20 m windows. In the 3 press phases where A faces the camera at F420-F441, the reference's four separated arcs now show.

MAJOR (crystal belt): I measured before changing anything. The swarm is the 18 authored crystals at every tier: belt A at 3.26 m and belt B at 3.86 m, both centred 0.2 m in front of the orb. A CPU model of SHARD_VERT checked every belt phase against ring A's opened bounding sphere (3.035 m). Only belt A's crystals behind the orb come near the opened quarters. The uniform 15 % widening was the smallest uniform value that kept them out, but it also pushed belt B and every crystal outward across the view, where the reference's crystals sit close around the arcs.

The hold rate is not the cause, so shardSlow stays 0.5. Speed relative to crystal size is 0.72-0.87 in the engine vs 0.69 in the reference, and the drop from rest to hold is 0.67-0.81 vs 0.73-0.82.

The fix (P2B_F1, the new default) gives each belt its own widening across the view and in depth, scaled by the opening: belt A +8 % / +20 %, belt B -10 % / +30 %. Across the view both belts end at the same 3.77 m, just outside the opened arcs; in the artist's .blend the two belts also share one radius. The extra depth keeps the belts apart where they cross. Every crystal now stays outside ring A's opened sphere at any ring orientation (model: +0.08 m, against +0.02 m for the uniform widening), and the two belts' crystals never overlap in the opened hold (the hotfix belt overlaps in 182 of 7532 ticks).

Same crystal phases, at the hotfix camera:
- Distance from the orb, p50 / p75 / p90: 375 / 464 / 543 px. Reference 386 / 459 / 477, hotfix 411 / 529 / 589, at judging time 500 / 635 / 717.
- Large crystals' on-screen speed: 23.9-24.4 px per frame. Reference 16.3, hotfix 27.3-28.0, at judging time 32.3.

`?spin=hf` restores the hotfix build exactly. Every older switch still matches. With the crystals hidden, the default hold is pixel-identical to the hotfix, so the rings, camera and environment are unchanged.

None of the judge's three nits is this lane's own defect (the rotating hold is a lead decision, the lunge timing belongs to the hold camera, the crystal look to the crystal owner), so they are unchanged. Both typechecks pass. I stopped my labs :5174 and :5194; :5173 and :3000 are still running. Nothing was committed, deployed or uploaded, and no .blend was touched. LOG.md has the dated record of every step, and HANDOFF.md has a new section 8 plus `?spin=hf` in section 2.
switches: ?spin=hf : the lead's hotfix build exactly: both crystal belts widened uniformly by 15 % with ring A's opening. 26 / 26 shots with the crystals visible and pinned match the hotfix build at mean 0.000; 2 pixels at p06 and 5 pixels at p05 differ by 1-9 levels.

Unchanged and re-checked against a frozen copy of the hotfix build (:5194, app identical to MAIN's), crystals visible and pinned: ?spin=p2b 11/12, ?spin=f2 15/16, ?hold=r10 15/16, ?spin=s3 12/12. The one differing shot in each run is live_F358_t1.1, the documented harness flicker (camera matrices differ by 1.3e-4, ring quaternions equal).
Runtime: __hero.debug.holdSpin.shardOutA = [across, depth] (default [0.08, 0.20]) and shardOutB (default [-0.10, 0.30]), both multiplied by the opening driver spreadA.

In the opened hold the two belts' crystals never overlap: clearance >= +0.015 m over 7532 ticks, where the hotfix belt overlaps in 182 ticks (-0.184 m).

?spin=hf vs the hotfix: 26/26 shots at mean 0.000. ?spin=p2b, ?spin=f2, ?hold=r10, ?spin=s3: identical except the known F358 harness-flicker shot.
T0 and T2 load, hold and release with the new belt and with ?spin=hf; no page errors in any run. Both typechecks exit 0 with no output.

This lane's parts are fixed: A never closes (5 press phases), the four-arc open frame shows whenever A faces the camera (tau 0 / 1.3 / 3.3 at F420-F441), and the crystals sit at the reference's distance from the orb. Still a FAIL because the rotating hold does not reproduce the reference's slab arrangement (lead decision 09:07, judge nit 3); not changed here.

open_issues: The crystals' look (only 18 crystals of one size, so on-screen size means nearness) keeps the large near crystals about 1.5x the reference's on-screen speed (24 vs 16.3 px per frame) and leaves 22 % of the crystal area beyond 477 px (reference 10 %). This is the judge's pre-existing nit 5 and belongs to the crystal owner.
The rotating hold does not reproduce State 2 to 5's slab arrangement (lead decision 09:07, judge nit 3). The four-arc open frame shows only when A's tumble faces the camera; A never closes.
The hold camera's lunge timing (judge nit 4) belongs to the hold lane and is unchanged.
The engine's crystal belt at rest sits closer to the orb than the reference's (judge srad p50 223 vs 266-271 px). Out of scope and unchanged.
Performance was not re-timed: the machine's 1-min load reached 109 during this round. The change is one per-belt uniform lookup in the crystal vertex shader and a few multiplies per frame on the CPU.

The merge into MAIN should take this lane's HoldR11.ts, Shards.ts, HeroEngine.ts and README.md; CameraRig.ts and Rings.ts already equal MAIN's. hero-lab/dist and tsconfig.tsbuildinfo are git-ignored build output.
